profile.name: Tianzheng Miao
profile.institution: KU Leuven, Ghent and Aalst Campuses
profile.bio: I explore how machine learning can make distributed wireless networks work better in the real world. My research connects physical-layer signal processing, cell-free massive MIMO, and experiments on real hardware, and currently extends to AI-RAN and O-RAN during an industrial secondment at IS-Wireless.
about: I am currently pursuing a Ph.D. in the Department of Electrical Engineering (ESAT) at KU Leuven under the supervision of [Prof. François Rottenberg](https://francoisrottenberg.dramco.be). Prior to this, I earned a B.Eng. in Telecommunication Engineering from [Xidian University](https://en.xidian.edu.cn/), Xi’an, China, in 2022, and an M.Phil. in Computer and Information Engineering from [The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen](https://www.cuhk.edu.cn/en), China, in 2024, under the supervision of [Prof. Rui Zhang](https://sse.cuhk.edu.cn/en/faculty/zhangrui).

As part of the [EMPOWER-6G](https://www.empower6g.eu) project, my research focuses on designing and implementing physical layer (PHY) mechanisms to enable cell-free (CF) networking using real channel data from the KU Leuven testbed ([Techtile](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/9815696)). Additionally, I am investigating dynamic algorithms for optimizing cooperation levels between DUs and APs, aiming to minimize interference at the regional edge while maintaining computational complexity at the CPU within practical limits.

I have now joined [IS-Wireless](https://www.is-wireless.com/) as a Junior Research Engineer in the Research and Innovation Department, to carry out the 18-month industrial secondment of the second phase of EMPOWER-6G. Working closely with industry, I study AI-RAN and O-RAN, focusing on how distributed units (DUs) and radio units (RUs) can cooperate under practical constraints: limited fronthaul capacity and inter-user interference. This builds on the physical-layer signal-processing research of the first phase of my Ph.D. and extends its scope from Layer 1 to Layers 1 and 2, covering the low-PHY, high-PHY, MAC and RLC, and potentially also PDCP and RRC.

gnn.title: GNN-based Precoder Design and Fine-tuning for Cell-free Massive MIMO with Real-world CSI
gnn.overview: Cell-free massive MIMO aims to provide uniform, high-quality wireless service through distributed access points. This work trains a graph neural network precoder on synthetic channel state information (CSI), then fine-tunes it with real measurements from the Techtile testbed.

results: Real channel measurements were collected at 500 spatial positions on the Techtile testbed, which has 33 ceiling-mounted access points; the positions produce diverse user combinations.
Fine-tuning improves the real-world sum rate by 8.2 bits/channel use (approximately 15.7%).
Freezing four layers yields the best performance among the layer-freezing strategies evaluated.
The fine-tuned model generalizes better than conjugate beamforming (CB) and performs close to zero-forcing (ZF) in practice.

compression_questions: How can fronthaul communication overhead be reduced while retaining useful information for downstream processing?
How should processing and cooperation be shared across access points, distributed units, and the central processor?
How can communication efficiency be considered alongside interference and practical computational complexity?
